Hi Kate — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can model cost and sizing for your team: 

Summary of call:
- Use case: invoice ingestion + generative summaries and line-item extraction for downstream reconciliation.
- Expected traffic pattern: bursty at month-end with steady baseline during month (see rough numbers below).
- Hard requirement: <250ms 95th latency for summaries on priority workflows.

Questions we need answers to to produce a target $/1M tokens estimate: 
1) Monthly token volumes (avg + 95th percentile/day). You mentioned ~3M/month baseline and spikes ~10–12M/day at month-end — can you confirm?
2) Target per-1M token cost (the number you think is achievable/acceptable) and overall monthly budget range. You referenced a budget conversation — any guardrails?
3) Expected concurrency for real-time flows (typical simultaneous requests during baseline and spikes).
4) Acceptable batching tradeoffs (we support continuous batching; are 100–250ms extra queuing delays acceptable if it reduces unit cost?)

I attached a rough pricing workbook (pricing-model-rough.xlsx) and a sample SOW template. Once we have the volume + concurrency answers I'll run a few unit-economics scenarios (tokens -> cost with batching + concurrency assumptions) and propose a starter Dedicated config or Hosted routing mix.

Next steps: if you can reply with the numbers below, I’ll turn this into a short summary deck for your CTO and ops team by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Camila

Hi Camila — great to chat. Answers inline below: 

> 1) Monthly token volumes
We’re seeing ~3.2M tokens/month right now (baseline) across our staging and prod combined. Month-end processing runs push us up to ~10–12M tokens/day for a 48–72 hour window. So baseline steady-state ~100k tokens/day, month-end spike ~10–12M/day.

> 2) Target per-1M token cost / budget
Our finance team has signaled a target operating cost of ~$150–$250 per 1M tokens processed (including embeddings + gen) for production workloads. For POC we can tolerate higher. Overall budget: $6k–$15k/month depending on quality/latency tradeoffs.

> 3) Expected concurrency
Baseline: ~3–8 concurrent requests for real-time summaries. Month-end: could see bursts of 50–80 concurrent requests for short windows. Background batch jobs run with higher parallelism but are not latency-sensitive.

> 4) Acceptable batching tradeoffs
We are open to continuous batching if it doesn’t push tail latency past ~400ms for priority requests. For non-priority/background jobs, queuing of several seconds is fine.

Hope that helps. Happy to sync again if you need more precision on tokenization metrics (we can share sample payloads).

—Kate

Thanks for the forward, Camila — ran a few back-of-envelope scenarios against Kate's numbers. Assumptions I used:
- Model: rw-medium-v1 (production), throughput ~120 tokens/sec per GPU with continuous batching optimizations; cheaper variants for background jobs.
- Continuous batching: average effective throughput improvement 2.5x vs 1:1 single-request execution at steady-state for small inputs (our stats). Peak packing efficiency reduces during very high concurrency but still provides benefits depending on request size.
- Concurrency handled by autoscaling pools; Dedicated recommended if they want strict latency SLOs during month-end spikes without cross-tenant interference.

Scenario A — Hosted with smart routing + continuous batching (mix of cached prefixes):
- Baseline 3.2M/month -> approx 106k tokens/day -> ~0.35M tokens/day equiv GPU-seconds after batching economics -> estimated cost: ~$200/1M tokens (within Kate's target) if we use batching and quantized variants for background flows.
- Month-end spikes (10–12M/day): If we rely on Hosted autoscaling, tail latency can hit their 400ms limit unless we provision for burst capacity. For Hosted, estimated unit cost for spike window ~ $180–$260/1M tokens depending on peak packing; still in target but tight on latency.

Scenario B — Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs sized for predictable month-end capacity):
- Upfront monthly commit increases base cost but brings down unit cost to ~$120–$170/1M tokens at their volumes, and gives stronger latency isolation (e.g., 250ms 95th achievable with proper pool sizing).

Recommendations:
1) For POC: Start on Hosted with continuous batching + warm standby Dedicated plan for month-end (can route spikes to Dedicated or higher-priority pool). This keeps near-term cost predictable and lets us validate packing efficiency.
2) If they need steady-state cost closer to $150/1M tokens, plan a Dedicated commit sized to cover ~60–70% of month-end burstable load.
3) Define explicit SLOs and run a short load test during POC to measure packing efficiency and real-world tail latency.

I’ll attach a quick calc snapshot to the Drive file. Happy to join a call with Kate and ops to walk through numbers.

-Marissa
